routes.label: Find the prices satisfying both comparisons

question:
A shopper plans to purchase an item that has a listed price greater than \(\$100\) and can use any one of the three coupons. Coupon A gives \(15\%\) off the listed price, Coupon B gives \(\$30\) off the listed price, and Coupon C gives \(25\%\) off the amount by which the listed price exceeds \(\$100.\)

Let \(x\) and \(y\) be the smallest and largest prices, respectively, for which Coupon A saves at least as many dollars as Coupon B or C. What is \(y - x?\)
solution:
Let \(p>100\) be the listed price in dollars. The savings from Coupons A, B, and C are respectively
\[0.15p,\qquad30,\qquad0.25(p-100).\]
For Coupon A to save at least as much as either alternative, both comparisons must hold:
\[0.15p\ge30\quad\text{and}\quad0.15p\ge0.25(p-100).\]
The first inequality gives \(p\ge200\). For the second,
\[0.15p\ge0.25p-25\]
becomes \(25\ge0.10p\), so \(p\le250\).

Consequently the qualifying prices are exactly
\[200\le p\le250.\]
They all satisfy \(p>100\). Because “at least” permits ties, both endpoints qualify. Thus \(x=200\), \(y=250\), and
\[y-x=250-200=\boxed{50},\]
choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
